Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 113, verses 1–5:

The meaning of His, may His remembrance be exalted and His names be sanctified, saying: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak (1) from the evil of what He has created (2) and from the evil of the darkness when it settles (3) and from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) and from the evil of the envier when he envies (5)﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, "I seek refuge (ista'ija) with the Lord of the daybreak from the evil of what He has created among the creatures."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed over the meaning of ﴿al-falaq﴾. Some of them said: it is a prison in Hell called by this name.

Those who said this:

- Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan told me, he said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb told us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: a prison in Hell.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb told us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿al-falaq﴾: a prison in Hell.

- Ya'qub told me, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: al-Awwam ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Julani informed us, he said: A man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Syria. He looked at the houses of the dhimmis (protected non-Muslims) and at what they were in of ease and brightness, and of the abundance granted to them in their worldly life. He said: "Woe to you! Is not behind them the falaq?" It was said: "And what is the falaq?" He said: "A house in Hell; when it is opened, the people of the Fire cry out."

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: I heard al-Suddi say: ﴿al-falaq﴾: a well in Hell.

- Ali ibn Hasan al-Azdi told me, he said: al-Ash'ari told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

- Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti told me, he said: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan al-Wasiti told us, he said: Nasr ibn Khuzayma al-Khurasani told us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The falaq: a well in Hell, covered."

- Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Nafi' ibn Yazid told us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Usayd told us, from Ibn Ajlan, from Abu Ubayd, from Ka'b, that he entered a church and was impressed by its beauty, and said: "Most excellent work, and most misguided people! I am pleased for you with the falaq." It was said: "And what is the falaq?" He said: "A house in Hell; when it is opened, all the people of the Fire cry out from the intensity of its heat."

Others said: it is one of the names of Hell.

Those who said this:

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I heard Khaytham ibn Abd Allah say: I asked Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli about ﴿al-falaq﴾, and he said: "It is Hell."

Others said: al-falaq is the dawn (al-subh).

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the dawn.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, he said: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the dawn.

- He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the dawn.

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us; and Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, both from Sufyan, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

- Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi told me, he said: al-Ash'ari told us, from Sufyan, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the dawn.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Salih told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, the like of it.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed us, from al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾: "He means the Splitter of the seed and the date-stone," and he said: "the Splitter of the dawn."

- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, he said: the dawn.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the splitting of the day.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the splitting of the dawn.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾: It was said to him: "The splitting of the dawn?" He said: "Yes," and he recited: ﴿Splitter of the dawn, and He made the night a rest﴾.

Others said: ﴿al-falaq﴾ means the creation, and the meaning of the statement is: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the creation."

Those who said this:

- Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿al-falaq﴾: he means: the creation.

The correct view on this matter is to say: Allah, mighty is His praise, commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to say ﴿I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾. In the speech of the Arabs, al-falaq is the splitting of the dawn; the Arabs say: "He is clearer than the splitting (falaq) of the dawn and the parting (farq) of the dawn." It is permissible that there be in Hell a prison named Falaq. If that is so, and Allah, mighty is His praise, has not placed any indication that by His saying ﴿the Lord of the falaq﴾ He meant some of what is called falaq and not others, and since Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is the Lord of everything He has created, it is necessary that all that is named falaq be meant by it, since He is the Lord of all of that.

And His saying, mighty is His praise: ﴿from the evil of what He has created﴾, because He commanded His Prophet to seek refuge ﴿from the evil of everything﴾, since everything other than Him is what He created.

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾.

He says: and from the evil of the dark one when it enters and advances upon us with its darkness.

Then the people of ta'wil differed over what is meant by the dark one in this verse, from which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge. Some of them said: it is the night when it grows dark.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the night.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, he said: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the beginning of the night when it grows dark.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Abu Sakhr told us, that al-Qurazi used to say regarding ﴿the darkness when it settles﴾: it is the day when it enters into the night.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the setting of the sun when the night comes, when it settles.

- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying ﴿the darkness﴾, he said: the night; ﴿when it settles﴾, he said: when it enters.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the night when it comes.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it comes.

- Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying ﴿when it settles﴾, he means: when it comes. Some of them said: it is the day when it enters into the night, and we have mentioned it before.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the setting of the sun when the night comes, when it wajaba (sets).

Others said: it is a star. Some of them used to say: that star is al-Thurayya (the Pleiades).

Those who said this:

- Mujahid ibn Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Hibban informed us, from Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayra, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: a star.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: The Arabs used to say: "The darkness (al-ghasiq) is the setting of al-Thurayya, and diseases and plagues would multiply at its setting and be lifted at its rising."

The proponent of this view has a basis from what was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), which is:

- Nasr ibn Ali told us, with it, he said: Bakkar ibn Abd Allah, the nephew of Hammam, told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: "The darkening star (al-najm al-ghasiq)."

Others said: rather, the darkness when it settles is the moon, and they related this as a report from the Prophet (ﷺ).

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us; and Ibn Sufyan told us, he said: My father told us and Yazid ibn Harun, with it.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from his maternal uncle al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand, then looked at the moon, then said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the darkness when it settles, and this is the darkness when it settles." This is the wording of the hadith of Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki'. As for Ibn Humayd, he said in his narration: She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "Do you know what this is? Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

- Muhammad ibn Sinan told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, from al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who looked at the moon and said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

The most correct of these sayings in my view, is to say: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to seek refuge ﴿from the evil of the darkness﴾, which is what grows dark. It is said: "The night has become dark (ghasaqa al-layl), yaghsuqu, ghusuqan," when it grows dark. ﴿When it settles﴾ means: when it enters into its darkness. The night when it enters into its darkness is dark (ghasiq), the star when it sets is dark, and the moon is dark when it settles. He did not restrict that to some of these, but the command was general, so every darkness, he (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from its evil when it settles. He used to say, regarding the meaning of waqaba: "It went away (dhahaba)."

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it goes away. I do not know what Qatada said about this in the speech of the Arabs; rather, the known meaning of waqaba in their speech is: "it entered."

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾.

He says: and from the evil of the sorceresses who blow into the knots of the thread when they perform incantations over them.

The people of ta'wil said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas [[Hadith 193 - This is a sound chain, and some of this hadith will also come with this chain at 207. Its takhrij will come at 195.]], ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: what is mixed with sorcery of incantations.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the sorceresses and the sorcerers.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, he said: Qatada recited: "and from the evil of the blowers in knots," and said: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery of these incantations."

- He said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, he said: Nothing is closer to shirk than the incantation of madmen.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, he said: al-Hasan used to say when he came to ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery."

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrima, ﴿the blowers in knots﴾, he said: Mujahid said: the incantations in the knots of the thread; and Ikrima said: the taking (of the thread) in the knots of the thread.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the blowers are the sorceresses in the knots.

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the envier from whose envy's evil the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge. Some of them said: it is every envier from whose evil of his eye and self the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: from the evil of his eye and his self, and from Ata al-Khurasani the like of that. Mu'ammar said: I heard Ibn Tawus narrate from his father, he said: "The eye is real, and if anything could outrun the decree, the eye would outrun it. And when one of you is asked to wash (istughsila), let him wash."[[Hadith 194 - This is also a sound chain. Abbad ibn Habish, with an unpointed ha' and a bah with one dot, and ending with a shin with dots, al-Kufi; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/78. Some of this hadith will also come at 208 with this chain.]]

Others said: rather, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded by this verse to seek refuge from the evil of the Jews who envied him.

Those who said this:

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: "The Jews; nothing prevented them from believing in him except their envy."

The more correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of every envier when he envies, when he blames him, or bewitches him, or seeks harm for him.

We only said that this is more correct because Allah, mighty and majestic, did not specify from His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾ one envier over another, but rather His command to him to seek refuge from the evil of every envier is general, so it stands on its generality.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Falaq.

- Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi told me, he said: al-Ash'ari told us, from Sufyan, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the dawn.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Salih told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, the like of it.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, he said: ﴿al-falaq﴾: the splitting of the dawn.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾: It was said to him: "The splitting of the dawn?" He said: "Yes," and he recited: ﴿Splitter of the dawn, and He made the night a rest﴾.

And His saying, mighty is His praise: ﴿from the evil of what He has created﴾, because He commanded His Prophet to seek refuge ﴿from the evil of everything﴾, since everything other than Him is what He created.

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾.

He says: and from the evil of the dark one when it enters and advances upon us with its darkness.

Then the people of ta'wil differed over what is meant by the dark one in this verse, from which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge. Some of them said: it is the night when it grows dark.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the night.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, he said: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the beginning of the night when it grows dark.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Abu Sakhr told us, that al-Qurazi used to say regarding ﴿the darkness when it settles﴾: it is the day when it enters into the night.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the setting of the sun when the night comes, when it settles.

- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying ﴿the darkness﴾, he said: the night; ﴿when it settles﴾, he said: when it enters.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the night when it comes.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it comes.

- Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying ﴿when it settles﴾, he means: when it comes. Some of them said: it is the day when it enters into the night, and we have mentioned it before.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the setting of the sun when the night comes, when it wajaba (sets).

Others said: it is a star. Some of them used to say: that star is al-Thurayya (the Pleiades).

Those who said this:

- Mujahid ibn Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Hibban informed us, from Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayra, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: a star.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: The Arabs used to say: "The darkness (al-ghasiq) is the setting of al-Thurayya, and diseases and plagues would multiply at its setting and be lifted at its rising."

The proponent of this view has a basis from what was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), which is:

- Nasr ibn Ali told us, with it, he said: Bakkar ibn Abd Allah, the nephew of Hammam, told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: "The darkening star (al-najm al-ghasiq)."

Others said: rather, the darkness when it settles is the moon, and they related this as a report from the Prophet (ﷺ).

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us; and Ibn Sufyan told us, he said: My father told us and Yazid ibn Harun, with it.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from his maternal uncle al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand, then looked at the moon, then said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the darkness when it settles, and this is the darkness when it settles." This is the wording of the hadith of Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki'. As for Ibn Humayd, he said in his narration: She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "Do you know what this is? Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

- Muhammad ibn Sinan told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, from al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who looked at the moon and said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

The most correct of these sayings in my view, is to say: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to seek refuge ﴿from the evil of the darkness﴾, which is what grows dark. It is said: "The night has become dark (ghasaqa al-layl), yaghsuqu, ghusuqan," when it grows dark. ﴿When it settles﴾ means: when it enters into its darkness. The night when it enters into its darkness is dark (ghasiq), the star when it sets is dark, and the moon is dark when it settles. He did not restrict that to some of these, but the command was general, so every darkness, he (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from its evil when it settles. He used to say, regarding the meaning of waqaba: "It went away (dhahaba)."

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it goes away. I do not know what Qatada said about this in the speech of the Arabs; rather, the known meaning of waqaba in their speech is: "it entered."

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾.

He says: and from the evil of the sorceresses who blow into the knots of the thread when they perform incantations over them.

The people of ta'wil said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas [[Hadith 193 - This is a sound chain, and some of this hadith will also come with this chain at 207. Its takhrij will come at 195.]], ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: what is mixed with sorcery of incantations.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the sorceresses and the sorcerers.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, he said: Qatada recited: "and from the evil of the blowers in knots," and said: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery of these incantations."

- He said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, he said: Nothing is closer to shirk than the incantation of madmen.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, he said: al-Hasan used to say when he came to ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery."

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrima, ﴿the blowers in knots﴾, he said: Mujahid said: the incantations in the knots of the thread; and Ikrima said: the taking (of the thread) in the knots of the thread.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the blowers are the sorceresses in the knots.

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the envier from whose envy's evil the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge. Some of them said: it is every envier from whose evil of his eye and self the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: from the evil of his eye and his self, and from Ata al-Khurasani the like of that. Mu'ammar said: I heard Ibn Tawus narrate from his father, he said: "The eye is real, and if anything could outrun the decree, the eye would outrun it. And when one of you is asked to wash (istughsila), let him wash."[[Hadith 194 - This is also a sound chain. Abbad ibn Habish, with an unpointed ha' and a bah with one dot, and ending with a shin with dots, al-Kufi; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/78. Some of this hadith will also come at 208 with this chain.]]

Others said: rather, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded by this verse to seek refuge from the evil of the Jews who envied him.

Those who said this:

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: "The Jews; nothing prevented them from believing in him except their envy."

The more correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of every envier when he envies, when he blames him, or bewitches him, or seeks harm for him.

We only said that this is more correct because Allah, mighty and majestic, did not specify from His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾ one envier over another, but rather His command to him to seek refuge from the evil of every envier is general, so it stands on its generality.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Falaq.

- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying ﴿the darkness﴾, he said: the night; ﴿when it settles﴾, he said: when it enters.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: the night when it comes.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it comes.

- Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying ﴿when it settles﴾, he means: when it comes. Some of them said: it is the day when it enters into the night, and we have mentioned it before.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the setting of the sun when the night comes, when it wajaba (sets).

Others said: it is a star. Some of them used to say: that star is al-Thurayya (the Pleiades).

Those who said this:

- Mujahid ibn Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Hibban informed us, from Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayra, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: a star.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: The Arabs used to say: "The darkness (al-ghasiq) is the setting of al-Thurayya, and diseases and plagues would multiply at its setting and be lifted at its rising."

The proponent of this view has a basis from what was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), which is:

- Nasr ibn Ali told us, with it, he said: Bakkar ibn Abd Allah, the nephew of Hammam, told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: "The darkening star (al-najm al-ghasiq)."

Others said: rather, the darkness when it settles is the moon, and they related this as a report from the Prophet (ﷺ).

- Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki' told us; and Ibn Sufyan told us, he said: My father told us and Yazid ibn Harun, with it.

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from his maternal uncle al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand, then looked at the moon, then said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the darkness when it settles, and this is the darkness when it settles." This is the wording of the hadith of Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki'. As for Ibn Humayd, he said in his narration: She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "Do you know what this is? Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

- Muhammad ibn Sinan told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, from al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who looked at the moon and said: "O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."

The most correct of these sayings in my view, is to say: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to seek refuge ﴿from the evil of the darkness﴾, which is what grows dark. It is said: "The night has become dark (ghasaqa al-layl), yaghsuqu, ghusuqan," when it grows dark. ﴿When it settles﴾ means: when it enters into its darkness. The night when it enters into its darkness is dark (ghasiq), the star when it sets is dark, and the moon is dark when it settles. He did not restrict that to some of these, but the command was general, so every darkness, he (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from its evil when it settles. He used to say, regarding the meaning of waqaba: "It went away (dhahaba)."

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: when it goes away. I do not know what Qatada said about this in the speech of the Arabs; rather, the known meaning of waqaba in their speech is: "it entered."

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾.

He says: and from the evil of the sorceresses who blow into the knots of the thread when they perform incantations over them.

The people of ta'wil said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas [[Hadith 193 - This is a sound chain, and some of this hadith will also come with this chain at 207. Its takhrij will come at 195.]], ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: what is mixed with sorcery of incantations.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the sorceresses and the sorcerers.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, he said: Qatada recited: "and from the evil of the blowers in knots," and said: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery of these incantations."

- He said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, he said: Nothing is closer to shirk than the incantation of madmen.

- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, he said: al-Hasan used to say when he came to ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾: "Beware of what is mixed with sorcery."

- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrima, ﴿the blowers in knots﴾, he said: Mujahid said: the incantations in the knots of the thread; and Ikrima said: the taking (of the thread) in the knots of the thread.

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾, he said: the blowers are the sorceresses in the knots.

* *

His saying: ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the envier from whose envy's evil the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge. Some of them said: it is every envier from whose evil of his eye and self the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: from the evil of his eye and his self, and from Ata al-Khurasani the like of that. Mu'ammar said: I heard Ibn Tawus narrate from his father, he said: "The eye is real, and if anything could outrun the decree, the eye would outrun it. And when one of you is asked to wash (istughsila), let him wash."[[Hadith 194 - This is also a sound chain. Abbad ibn Habish, with an unpointed ha' and a bah with one dot, and ending with a shin with dots, al-Kufi; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/78. Some of this hadith will also come at 208 with this chain.]]

Others said: rather, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded by this verse to seek refuge from the evil of the Jews who envied him.

Those who said this:

- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾, he said: "The Jews; nothing prevented them from believing in him except their envy."

The more correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of every envier when he envies, when he blames him, or bewitches him, or seeks harm for him.

We only said that this is more correct because Allah, mighty and majestic, did not specify from His saying ﴿and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾ one envier over another, but rather His command to him to seek refuge from the evil of every envier is general, so it stands on its generality.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Falaq.
